arxiv-1411-0416.title: Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Epidemic Phenomena Using the \proglang R Package \pkg surveillance
arxiv-1411-0416.creator: Sebastian Meyer University of Zurich, Leonhard Held University of Zurich, Michael Höhle Stockholm University
arxiv-1411-0416.description: Abstract \Plainauthor Sebastian Meyer, Leonhard Held, Michael Höhle \Plaintitle Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Epidemic Phenomena Using the R Package surveillance \Shorttitle \pkg surveillance: Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Epidemic Phenomena \Abstract The availability of geocoded health data and the inherent temporal structure of communicable diseases have led to an increased interest in statistical models and software for spatio-temporal data with epidemic features.

arxiv-1903-02209.title: Measurement of prompt photon production in s NN = 8.16 \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16 TeV p p +Pb collisions with ATLAS
arxiv-1903-02209.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1903-02209.description: Abstract The inclusive production rates of isolated, prompt photons in p p +Pb collisions at s NN = 8.16 \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16 TeV are studied with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider using a dataset with an integrated luminosity of 165 165 nb -1 recorded in 2016.

arxiv-2207-03378.title: Small- x x evolution of the gluon GPD E g E_{g}
arxiv-2207-03378.creator: Yoshitaka Hatta, Jian Zhou
arxiv-2207-03378.description: Abstract We study the small- x x evolution equation for the gluon generalized parton distribution (GPD) E g E_{g} of the nucleon. It is shown that E g E_{g} at vanishing skewness exhibits the Regge behavior identical to the BFKL Pomeron despite its association with nucleon helicity-flip processes.

arxiv-2302-07587.title: Lipschitz-volume rigidity of Lipschitz manifolds among integral currents
arxiv-2302-07587.creator: Roger Züst
arxiv-2302-07587.description: Abstract . We give sufficient conditions such that a volume preserving 1-Lipschitz map from a metric integral current onto an infinitesimally Euclidean Lipschitz manifold is an isometry. 1. Introduction The main question investigated in this note is the following: Suppose (X,d_{X},\mu_{X}) and (Y,d_{Y},\mu_{Y}) are metric measure spaces and f:X\to Y is onto, 1 -Lipschitz and measure preserving.

arxiv-2304-12275.title: Central limit theorem for smooth statistics of one-dimensional free fermions
arxiv-2304-12275.creator: Alix Deleporte, Gaultier Lambert
arxiv-2304-12275.description: Abstract We consider the determinantal point processes associated with the spectral projectors of a Schrödinger operator on ℝ \mathbb{R} , with a smooth confining potential. In the semiclassical limit, where the number of particles tends to infinity, we obtain a Szegő-type central limit theorem (CLT) for the fluctuations of smooth linear statistics.

arxiv-2306-02856.title: All-Optical Ultrafast Valley Switching in Two-Dimensional Materials
arxiv-2306-02856.creator: Navdeep Rana, Gopal Dixit
arxiv-2306-02856.description: Abstract Electrons in two-dimensional materials possess an additional quantum attribute, the valley pseudospin, labelled as 𝐊 \mathbf{K} and 𝐊 ′ \mathbf{K}^{\prime} – analogous to the spin up and spin down. The majority of research to achieve valley-selective excitations in valleytronics depends on resonant circularly-polarised light with a given helicity.

arxiv-2403-17588.title: Forest-ORE : Mining Optimal Rule Ensemble to interpret Random Forest models
arxiv-2403-17588.creator: Haddouchi Maissae, Berrado Abdelaziz
arxiv-2403-17588.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Haddouchi Maissae, Berrado Abdelaziz. Random Forest (RF) is well-known as an efficient ensemble learning method in terms of predictive performance. It is also considered a “black box” because of its hundreds of deep decision trees. This lack of interpretability can be a real drawback for acceptance of RF models in several real-world applications, especially those affecting one’s lives, such as in healthcare, security, and law.

arxiv-2406-19521.title: A Thermal Study of Terahertz Induced Protein Interactions
arxiv-2406-19521.creator: Hadeel Elayan, Samar Elmaadawy, Andrew W. Eckford, Raviraj Adve, Josep Jornet
arxiv-2406-19521.description: Abstract Proteins can be regarded as thermal nanosensors in an intra-body network. Upon being stimulated by Terahertz (THz) frequencies that match their vibrational modes, protein molecules experience resonant absorption and dissipate their energy as heat, undergoing a thermal process. This paper aims to analyze the effect of THz signaling on the protein heat dissipation mechanism.

arxiv-2408-01203.title: Zoomable Level-of-Detail ChartTables for Interpreting Probabilistic Model Outputs for Reactionary Train Delays
arxiv-2408-01203.creator: Aidan Slingsby City, University of London, Jonathan Hyde Risk Solutions
arxiv-2408-01203.description: Abstract “Reactionary delay” is a result of the accumulated cascading effects of knock-on train delays which is increasing on UK railways due to increasing utilisation of the railway infrastructure. The chaotic nature of its effects on train lateness is notoriously hard to predict.

arxiv-2409-19522.title: Examining Exams Using Rasch Models and Assessment of Measurement Invariance
arxiv-2409-19522.creator: Achim Zeileis Universität Innsbruck
arxiv-2409-19522.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Achim Zeileis Universität Innsbruck. \Plainauthor

Achim Zeileis

\Shorttitle
Examining Exams

\Abstract
Many statisticians regularly teach large lecture courses on statistics,
probability, or mathematics for students from other fields such as business
and economics, social sciences and psychology, etc. The corresponding exams
often use a multiple-choice or single-choice format and are typically
evaluated and graded automatically, either by scanning printed exams or via
online learning management systems. Although further examinations of these
exams would be of interest, these are frequently not carried out.

arxiv-2501-18137.title: Tensor Completion for Surrogate Modeling of Material Property Prediction
arxiv-2501-18137.creator: Shaan Pakala, Dawon Ahn, Evangelos Papalexakis
arxiv-2501-18137.description: Abstract When designing materials to optimize certain properties, there are often many possible configurations of designs that need to be explored. For example, the materials’ composition of elements will affect properties such as strength or conductivity, which are necessary to know when developing new materials.

arxiv-2503-03841.title: In-sample calibration yields conformal calibration guarantees
arxiv-2503-03841.creator: Sam Allen, Georgios Gavrilopoulos, Alexander Henzi, Gian-Reto Kleger, Johanna Ziegel
arxiv-2503-03841.description: Abstract Conformal predictive systems allow forecasters to issue predictive distributions for real-valued future outcomes that have out-of-sample calibration guarantees. On a more abstract level, conformal prediction makes use of in-sample calibration guarantees to construct bands of predictions with out-of-sample guarantees under exchangeability. The calibration guarantees are typically that prediction intervals derived from the predictive distributions have the correct marginal coverage.

arxiv-2505-03322.title: Notes on su ( 1 , 2 ) ⊕ (1,2)\oplus u ( 1 ) (1) Chern-Simons theory and Torsional Newton-Cartan gravity
arxiv-2505-03322.creator: Yang Lei, ​​, Dong Zhang
arxiv-2505-03322.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate three-dimensional torsional Newton-Cartan (TNC) gravity by gauging the su ( 1 , 2 ) ⊕ (1,2)\oplus u ( 1 ) (1) algebra and construct its action using the Chern-Simons theory. This TNC exhibits novel features, including the fact that the gauge fields associated with both dilatation and rotation symmetries transform non-trivially under Galilean boosts.

pmc-11715422.creator: Oriol Grau‐Rivera, Gonzalo Sánchez‐Benavides, Marc Suárez‐Calvet, Juan Domingo Gispert, Karine Fauria, Carolina Minguillón, Jose Luis Molinuevo

pmc-12522375.creator: Huan Zhang, Yifei An, Min Song, Yingtao Meng
pmc-12522375.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTraditional risk assessment tools were commonly used for the prediction of falls in clinical practice. However, their tendency toward over-sensitivity addressed its limitations for hospitalized cancer patients. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with falls in hospitalized patients and to develop a predictive risk model using machine learning algorithms specifically for cancer patients, to optimize the clinical assessment of fall risk.MethodsUsing data from 298 cancer patients admitted to Shandong Cancer Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024 were included.

pmc-12769530.creator: Mohammed El-Amine Nouairi, Mohammed Freha
pmc-12769530.description: Nitrogen containing organic compounds such as pyridine are major industrial water pollutants that pose serious environmental and health risks. pmc-13584756.creator: Omeo Kumar Ghosh, Md Mazharul Islam, Fajilatun Nesa, Md Shaikat Hasan, Ashiqul Amin Abid, Syed Akhiar Ahsan Arham, Mohammad Shoeb, Md Iqbal Rouf Mamun
pmc-13584756.description: Pesticide contamination in dried fish presents a great food safety concern in Bangladesh. This study investigated the status of DDT and its metabolite levels in ninety‐six samples of two commercially available and widely consumed dried fish species, Harpadon nehereus and Trichiurus lepturus , collected across the country. The samples were extracted using the solid‐phase dispersion technique and analyzed by GC‐ECD.
